title: Checks for unnecessary generators that can be rewritten as list comprehensions (or with list() directly).
summary: It is unnecessary to use list() around a generator expression, since there are equivalent comprehensions for these types. Using a comprehension is clearer and more idiomatic. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-comprehensions and made it stable in v0.0.61.
message_templates: Unnecessary generator (rewrite using `list()`)
Unnecessary generator (rewrite as a list comprehension)

title: Checks for unnecessary generators that can be rewritten as set comprehensions (or with set() directly).
summary: It is unnecessary to use set around a generator expression, since there are equivalent comprehensions for these types. Using a comprehension is clearer and more idiomatic. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-comprehensions and made it stable in v0.0.61.
message_templates: Unnecessary generator (rewrite using `set()`)
Unnecessary generator (rewrite as a set comprehension)

title: Checks for unnecessary generators that can be rewritten as dict comprehensions.
summary: It is unnecessary to use dict() around a generator expression, since there are equivalent comprehensions for these types. Using a comprehension is clearer and more idiomatic. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-comprehensions and made it stable in v0.0.61.
message_templates: Unnecessary generator (rewrite as a dict comprehension)

title: Checks for unnecessary list comprehensions.
summary: It's unnecessary to use a list comprehension inside a call to set(), since there is an equivalent comprehension for this type. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-comprehensions and made it stable in v0.0.58.
message_templates: Unnecessary list comprehension (rewrite as a set comprehension)

title: Checks for unnecessary list comprehensions.
summary: It's unnecessary to use a list comprehension inside a call to dict(), since there is an equivalent comprehension for this type. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-comprehensions and made it stable in v0.0.58.
message_templates: Unnecessary list comprehension (rewrite as a dict comprehension)

title: Checks for set() calls that take unnecessary list or tuple literals as arguments.
summary: It's unnecessary to use a list or tuple literal within a call to set(). Instead, the expression can be rewritten as a set literal. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-comprehensions and made it stable in v0.0.61.
message_templates: Unnecessary {} literal (rewrite as a set literal)

title: Checks for unnecessary list or tuple literals.
summary: It's unnecessary to use a list or tuple literal within a call to dict(). It can be rewritten as a dict literal ({}). Ruff takes this rule from flake8-comprehensions and made it stable in v0.0.61.
message_templates: Unnecessary {} literal (rewrite as a dict literal)

title: Checks for unnecessary dict(), list() or tuple() calls that can be rewritten as empty literals.
summary: It's unnecessary to call, e.g., dict() as opposed to using an empty literal ({}). The former is slower because the name dict must be looked up in the global scope in case it has been rebound. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-comprehensions and made it stable in v0.0.61.
message_templates: Unnecessary `{}()` call (rewrite as a literal)

title: Checks for tuple calls that take unnecessary list or tuple literals as arguments.
summary: It's unnecessary to use a list or tuple literal within a tuple() call, since there is a literal syntax for these types. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-comprehensions and made it stable in v0.0.66.
message_templates: Unnecessary list literal passed to `tuple()` (rewrite as a tuple literal)
Unnecessary tuple literal passed to `tuple()` (remove the outer call to `tuple()`)

title: Checks for list() calls that take unnecessary list or tuple literals as arguments.
summary: It's unnecessary to use a list or tuple literal within a list() call, since there is a literal syntax for these types. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-comprehensions and made it stable in v0.0.66.

title: Checks for unnecessary list() calls around list comprehensions.
summary: It is redundant to use a list() call around a list comprehension. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-comprehensions and made it stable in v0.0.73.
message_templates: Unnecessary `list()` call (remove the outer call to `list()`)

title: Checks for unnecessary list() or reversed() calls around sorted() calls.
summary: It is unnecessary to use list() around sorted(), as the latter already returns a list. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-comprehensions and made it stable in v0.0.73.
message_templates: Unnecessary `{}()` call around `sorted()`

title: Checks for unnecessary list(), reversed(), set(), sorted(), and tuple() call within list(), set(), sorted(), and tuple() calls.
summary: It's unnecessary to double-cast or double-process iterables by wrapping the listed functions within an additional list(), set(), sorted(), or tuple() call. Doing so is redundant and can be confusing for readers. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-comprehensions and made it stable in v0.0.70.
message_templates: Unnecessary `{}()` call within `{}()`

title: Checks for unnecessary subscript reversal of iterable.
summary: It's unnecessary to reverse the order of an iterable when passing it into reversed(), set() or sorted() functions as they will change the order of the elements again. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-comprehensions and made it stable in v0.0.64.
message_templates: Unnecessary subscript reversal of iterable within `{}()`

title: Checks for unnecessary dict, list, and set comprehension.
summary: It's unnecessary to use a dict/list/set comprehension to build a data structure if the elements are unchanged. Wrap the iterable with dict(), list(), or set() instead. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-comprehensions and made it stable in v0.0.73.
message_templates: Unnecessary {} comprehension (rewrite using `{}()`)

title: Checks for unnecessary map() calls with lambda functions.
summary: Using map(func, iterable) when func is a lambda is slower than using a generator expression or a comprehension, as the latter approach avoids the function call overhead, in addition to being more readable. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-comprehensions and made it stable in v0.0.74.
message_templates: Unnecessary `map()` usage (rewrite using a {})

title: Checks for dict() calls that take unnecessary dict literals or dict comprehensions as arguments.
summary: It's unnecessary to wrap a dict literal or comprehension within a dict() call, since the literal or comprehension syntax already returns a dictionary. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-comprehensions and made it stable in v0.0.262.
message_templates: Unnecessary dict {} passed to `dict()` (remove the outer call to `dict()`)

title: Checks for unnecessary list or set comprehensions passed to builtin functions that take an iterable.
summary: Many builtin functions (this rule currently covers any and all in stable, along with min, max, and sum in preview) accept any iterable, including a generator. Constructing a temporary list via list comprehension is unnecessary and wastes memory for large iterables. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-comprehensions and made it stable in v0.0.262.
message_templates: Unnecessary list comprehension
Unnecessary set comprehension

title: Checks for unnecessary dict comprehension when creating a dictionary from an iterable.
summary: It's unnecessary to use a dict comprehension to build a dictionary from an iterable when the value is static. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-comprehensions and made it stable in 0.10.0.
message_templates: Unnecessary dict comprehension for iterable; use `dict.fromkeys` instead
